(1st award) | website = {{URL|ballondor.com}} | previous = [[2021 Ballon d'Or|2021]] | main = [[Ballon d'Or]] | next = [[2023 Ballon d'Or|2023]] }} The '''2022 Ballon d'Or''' ({{lit|'''2022 Golden Ball'''}}) was the 66th annual presentation of the [[Ballon d'Or]], presented by ''[[France Football]]'', recognising the best footballers in the world during the 2021–22 season. For the first time in the history of the award, it was given based on the results of the European season, instead of the calendar year.{{cite web |last=McVeigh |first=Niall |date=17 October 2022 |title=Alexia Putellas and Karim Benzema are crowned 2022 Ballon d'Or winners |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/oct/17/ballon-dor-2022-awards-karim-benzema-alexia-putellas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230101082542/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/oct/17/ballon-dor-2022-awards-karim-benzema-alexia-putellas |archive-date=1 January 2023 |accessdate=18 October 2022 |work=The Guardian}} The nominees for the ceremony were announced on 12 August 2022,{{Cite web |last=Spencer |first=Jamie |date=12 August 2022 |title=Ballon d'Or 2022: The confirmed 30-player shortlist |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/ballon-dor-2022-confirmed-30-player-shortlist |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812193827/https://www.90min.com/posts/ballon-dor-2022-confirmed-30-player-shortlist |archive-date=12 August 2022 |access-date=28 July 2023 |publisher=90min}} and the ceremony was held on 17 October.{{cite news |date=25 May 2022 |title=Le Ballon d'Or 2022 remis le 17 octobre prochain |language=fr |trans-title=The Ballon d'Or 2022 awarded on October 17 |work=L'Équipe |publisher= |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/France-Football/Actualites/Le-ballon-d-or-2022-remis-le-17-octobre-prochain/1334796 |url-status=live |access-date=18 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601132652/https://www.lequipe.fr/France-Football/Actualites/Le-ballon-d-or-2022-remis-le-17-octobre-prochain/1334796 |archive-date=1 June 2022}} [[Karim Benzema]] won the [[Ballon d'Or]], for successfully leading [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] to win both [[UEFA Champions League]] and [[La Liga]]. [[Alexia Putellas]] claimed the [[Ballon d'Or Féminin]], following her successful domestic campaign with [[FC Barcelona Femení|Barcelona]]. In the other award categories, [[Gavi (footballer)|Gavi]] was given the [[Kopa Trophy]], [[Thibaut Courtois]] won the [[Yashin Trophy]], [[Robert Lewandowski]] was presented the newly named [[Gerd Müller Trophy]], [[Sadio Mané]] was awarded the inaugural [[Sócrates Award]], and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] claimed the Club of the Year award. Reigning winner [[Lionel Messi]] was not nominated for the award for the first time since [[2005 Ballon d'Or|2005]].{{Cite web |date=2022-08-12 |title=Messi left off 30-man Ballon d'Or shortlist for first time since 2005 as Neymar also misses out |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/messi-left-off-30-man-ballon-d-or-shortlist-for-first-time-since-2005-as-neymar-also-misses-out/blt11a062433a90bb79 |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=Goal.com |language=en}} == Ballon d'Or == {{Main|Ballon d'Or}} Following a successful season with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Karim Benzema]] was awarded the 2022 [[Ballon d'Or]], finishing ahead of [[Sadio Mané]] in second place and [[Kevin De Bruyne]] in third. With his club, Benzema won the [[UEFA Champions League]] and the [[La Liga]] title.{{Cite web |last=Maston |first=Tom |date=17 October 2022 |title=How Benzema won the 2022 Ballon d'Or |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/how-benzema-won-ballon-dor-2022/bltbabd57f011b132dc#csd25372dfbfce476b |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604141542/https://www.goal.com/en/lists/how-benzema-won-ballon-dor-2022/bltbabd57f011b132dc |archive-date=4 June 2023 |access-date=27 July 2023 |publisher=Goal}} He was instrumental in the Spanish side's progress through the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]] of the Champions League, scoring crucial goals against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the semi-final legs, as well as netting [[hat-trick]]s against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the round of 16 and quarter-finals respectively. [[Édouard Mendy]].]] Belgian international [[Thibaut Courtois]] won the 2022 [[Yashin Trophy]], awarded to the best performing goalkeeper during the 2021–22 season. During a very successful campaign with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], he won both the [[UEFA Champions League]] and [[La Liga]] as a regular in the team, establishing himself as a prominent contender for the award. Aged 30 at the time of receiving the award, Courtois made the most saves of any goalkeeper featuring in the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League]]; during the competition's [[2022 UEFA Champions League final|final]] against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], he made nine saves and was named [[Player of the match|man of the match]]''.''{{Cite news |last=Johnson |first=Jonathan |date=28 May 2022 |title=Champions League final 2022: Thibaut Courtois' clutch saves cement Real Madrid's UCL winning pedigree |work=CBS Sports |url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/champions-league-final-2022-thibaut-courtois-clutch-saves-cement-real-madrids-ucl-winning-pedigree/ |url-status=live |access-date=19 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322074408/https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/champions-league-final-2022-thibaut-courtois-clutch-saves-cement-real-madrids-ucl-winning-pedigree/ |archive-date=22 March 2023}} Courtois won the award ahead of [[Alisson Becker|Alisson]] and [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]], who both shared the [[2021–22 Premier League]] [[Premier League Golden Glove|Golden Glove]]. After previously being known as the Striker of the Year award it was renamed as the Gerd Müller Trophy after German striker [[Gerd Müller]] died in August 2021. Lewandowski scored 57 goals in 56 matches, seven more than second placed [[Kylian Mbappé]]; he also finished fourth in the 2022 Ballon d'Or ranking, behind only [[Karim Benzema]], [[Sadio Mané]] and [[Kevin De Bruyne]]. club [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] won Club of the Year ahead of [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]]. With the most Ballon d'Or and Ballon d'Or Féminin player nominations, Manchester City succeeded [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] as the second club to win the award following the award's introduction in 2021. The club had [[João Cancelo]], [[Kevin De Bruyne]], [[Phil Foden]], [[Riyad Mahrez]] and [[Bernardo Silva]] nominated for the season's Ballon d'Or, following their [[Premier League]] triumph. Additionally, [[Lucy Bronze]], from [[Manchester City W.F.C.|Manchester City Women]], was nominated for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, totalling six players from the club.
